dialogue.text: A place where you'll never be bothered by your family again.
Marge, tell her how I don't push Ned around.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Actually, sometimes you do push Ned around.
Well, maybe you and the car got off on the wrong foot. When do you think things first went wrong?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: All right, I remember we all got in... and by the way, that backseat is pretty tight for the kids. I mean, I don't know what we'd do if we had another baby. With this car, we're basically saying no more babies!
... And then he worked on a machine to communicate with the dead. Some kind of scary telephone I guess. Or maybe he planned to just stick his head under the ground and yell.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: All right, already! Everyone knows the man accomplished a lot. Maybe because he didn't spend every waking moment talking about Thomas Edison!

Don't worry. I won't embarrass you. I will put my napkin in my lap. I will use the utensils provided for me. And if our food is slow in coming I will "blow my stack" in a manner befitting the Earl of Yarborough.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: All right, you've made your point.
Tell you what -- let's sleep on it. Okay?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: All right. But if anything happens...
And no TV!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: And I'm taking all the exciting colors out of your crayons!
No, Marge, I just can't. I mean, look at me. I'm a Trainee... They won't even tell me what's in the secret sauce. But I can't buy you a decent wedding ring.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Any ring is fine as long as it's from you.
And that "little while" is now eight years and counting. Heh heh heh.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Anyway, Bart had just entered the "terrible twos.
I have a great way to solve our money woes: you rent your womb to a rich, childless couple. If you agree, signify by getting indignant.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Are you crazy?! I'm not going to be a surrogate mother.
This is terrible. What am I gonna do?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Aren't you gonna come to bed, Homie?
Absolutely -- that unpleasantness in Ecuador is behind us, my coca leaf addiction is under control, and Bart is finally trapped in that paradise above the clouds.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Bart! Where are you, Bart?

And if you get kicked out of that one, you're going straight in the Army. Where you'll be sent straight to America's latest military quagmire. Where will it be? North Korea? Iran? Anything's possible with Commander Cuckoo Bananas in charge.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Bart, this could be a good new school... Oakwood Academy! Huh?
And why am I here?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Because the streets of Capitol City are no place for three unescorted ladies.
All right! Liver!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Boy, it sure would be fun to carpool in one of those, huh, kids? I'd be a real hot-rod mama, wouldn't I? Huh? Huh?
Marge, I believe we have a little unfinished business. Come with me!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Boy, that was worth the wait.
Ha ha! I got you. Don't try that. I got ya. I'll block you. And the crowd is on its feet as Hurricane Homer moves in for the kill.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Boys, I'd like your attention, please.
Oh, good. Because I do love you and I don't deserve you as much as a guy with a fat wallet and a credit card that won't set off that horrible beeping.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: But I think it does have something to do with your Christmas bonus. I keep asking for it, but...
This dude gets it.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: But the Van Houtens are our friends!
Honey, I've given this matter a lot of study. And of all the commercials I saw, his was the best. All it costs is two hundred and fifty dollars.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: But we don't have that kind of money.
Woo hoo! My springs! They finally came!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: But we lost the Olympics to Shelbyville.
...the smallest nesting doll!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Can you find anything you like in this bed?
Who said that?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Come on, Bart. While your dad gets his glasses, we'll go shop for your trip.
Stupid Flandish. Uh, listen, since all the other fun stuff is out of bounds, how 'bout a little Bible-thumping in the crow's nest? What do you say, Miss...

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Constance Prudence Chastity Goodfaith.
What the-- Where's my money?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Dear Homie, Had to buy diapers for Maggie. Love, Marge.
I don't understand anything! When they look up stupid in the dictionary, there'll be a picture of me!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Dear Lord, if you spare this town from becoming a smoking hole in the ground, I'll try to be a better Christian. I don't know what I can do... Ummm, oooh, the next time there's a canned food drive I'll give the poor something they'd actually like instead of old lima beans and pumpkin mix.
What? Why? Oh, yeah. Hello Patty, hello Selma. How was your trip?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Dear friends of the Simpson family: We had some sadness and some gladness this year. First the sadness. Our little cat, Snowball, was unexpectedly run over and went to kitty heaven. But we bought a new little cat, Snowball II...so I guess life goes on. Speaking of life going on, Grampa is still with us, feisty as ever. Maggie is walking by herself. Lisa got straight A's, and Bart, well... we love Bart. The magic of the season has touched us all...
I did it. I changed the world. Now I know exactly how God feels.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Do you want turkey sausage or ham?

Oh, it was delightful. The frosting on the cake was this thick. And Eugene Fisk, my poor sucker of an assistant, didn't know the fruit punch was spiked. And he really made an ass of himself putting the moves on the new girl in Valve Maintenance.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Does this girl like him?
Hee hee, I win! In your face! Yeah! How do you like them apples? Woo hoo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Don't gloat, Homer. You know, Bart, when I was your age, the one thing I wanted more than anything in the world was a Child-sized Electric Lightbulb Oven. My parents wouldn't give me the money, so I went to my sisters, Patty and Selma...
Oh no! Two-hundred and thirty-nine pounds. I'm a whale. Why was I was cursed with this weakness for snack treats? Well, from now on, exercise every morning, Homer.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Don't strain yourself, dear.
Excuse me. I have to make a call.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Don't take too long!
You're cooking what for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Everywhere I look, someone is breaking the law. Dog, no leash. Man littering. Horse not wearing diaper. Car parked across three handicapped spaces...
Grooming him, eh?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Ew, Homer, there is a bird on your head?
Lumber. We need lumber.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Excuse me, Mr. Szyslak, have you ever considered selling your home?
What a game! I got on the kiss-cam, I participated in "the wave," and I got to pee in a trough! Marge, can we get a trough?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: For the last time, no!
I'm fightin' for ya, babe. Fighting like I would for the last slice of cold pizza in the box. And to show you how serious I am...

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: From the gas station?
I'm all naked and wet!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Get up, Homer. It's time for church.
A heart-shaped box of chocolates.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Gil, listen. We've been very patient, but I want you to...
Well, Marge, it was horrible. Everyone was against me in that jury room. But I stood by the courage of my convictions and I prevailed. And that's why we had Chinese food for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Good for you, Homie. You know, a lot of things happened around here while you were gone.
Note to self: stop doing anything.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Has anyone seen Homer?
Hm, oh honey, one teensy problem with this plan. I'm a teensy bit concerned about them smoking around the children. You know, their lungs are so teensy.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: He has a point...
He can't remember my name!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: He's causing us all to yell!
to me.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Hello, everyone. You know, Halloween is a very strange holiday. Personally, I don't understand it. Kids worshiping ghosts, pretending to be devils... things on T.V. that are completely inappropriate for younger viewers. Things like the following half hour. Nothing seems to bother my kids, but tonight's show, which I totally wash my hands of, is really scary, so if you have sensitive children, maybe you should tuck them into bed early tonight, instead of writing us angry letters tomorrow. Thanks for your attention.
Oh, that takes me back.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Here it is, this week's family activity.
I needed my power fix.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Hey, listen to this!
Here you go.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Hmmm. And, Bart is set for the week.
Hurry up -- it's my first day of clown college.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Hold still, Homer. Don't squirm.
Yeah, Moe, that team sure did suck last night! They just plain sucked! I've seen teams suck before, but they were the suckiest bunch of sucks that ever sucked!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer! Watch your mouth!
So you lost my car, eh? Well, that's just grand. I ought to punch you in the nose, but I have to pick up my kids at school.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, I don't want you driving around in a car you built yourself.
What?! Oh my God, my sweet Margie! Okay, listen very carefully: don't do anything they say, remain panicky, and above all, try to be a hero.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, I have to go. If I don't make it, feel free to remarry -- from anyone on the list in the bulletin board in the closet.
Hey, Marge. How's my little piglet?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, I'm on duty.
Okay, okay, calm down.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, can you get the door? It's my sisters.
No, you listen! This is my wife and this is my kid, and I'm paying for this delivery, so if you want to stay, you better give me some respect!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, does this mean --
Well let's just call 'em uh, "Mr. X" and "Mrs. Y." So anyway, Mr. X would say, 'Marge, If this doesn't get your motor running, my name isn't Homer J. Simpson.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, don't you have to get to class?
Eat Marshall Tucker, idiot!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, is that you?!
Aw, Marge, we were so close to winning the championship. Now thanks to Burns it's never gonna happen. And I spent so much time building that trophy case.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, maybe Mr. Burns will bowl a great game and you will win your championship.
Lousy Democrats.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, of all the crazy ideas you've had, this one ranks somewhere in the middle. You're thirty-eight years old, you don't know how to box and you haven't gotten any exercise since grade school. Before you even consider this, I insist you consult a doctor.
C'mon, Marge. This place is great. Free admission, great grub and we got to use the bathroom of the future.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, that was Apollo Twelve!
Woo hoo! Free cheese!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, that was for the dog.
Dear Lord, bless this humble meal, and did you hear about Krusty? Whoa, man! I mean, I knew he was a player, but geez, a kid?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, that's not a prayer, that's gossip.
Well -- and I can explain, remember -- I fill the balls with beer that I found at the dump, then I bowl them and some underground pipes take them into Moe's.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, that's very clever!
I'm pathetic? Because I take money from my ten-year-old son? Well, let me tell you something: I still call the shots around here!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, use your inside voice.
I 'unno. Coast Guard?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, wasn't the whole point to catch the cat burglar?
Oh. My dreams will go unfulfilled! Oh no. I don't like the sound of that one bit. That means I have nothing to hope for. Marge, make it better. Please. Can't you make it better, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, when a man's biggest dreams include seconds on dessert, occasional snuggling, and sleeping till noon on weekends, no one man can destroy them.
Wow, a houseboat! You know, the great thing is if you don't like your neighbors, you can just pull up the anchor and sail someplace else.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, where's the dog?
THEY BURNED DOWN THE GAMBLING HOUSE - IT DIED WITH AN AWFUL SOUND / I AM HUNGRY FOR A CAN-DY BAR / I THINK I'LL EAT A "MOUNDS"...

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, you're doing drugs!
Here's our room!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, you're supposed to slide those doors open.
And now you're ready for a night on the town.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer, you've got it set on "Whore.
I'm ready to go to school.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer... you're not going to school.
Look what Maggie got!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homer? How did you get???
Oh, wait. That's Lisa's nose.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie! You're all right!
Only one hundred percent?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie, I love you, and I'm glad we're finally using our wedding china, but when you're helping to pick the next leader of the free world...
I recognized the logo.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie, are you okay?
Sleep well, Maggie. Ah, three for three.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie, did you straighten everything out???
Also, if you wanna find the real shooter of Mr. Burns, go back and look for more clues. They're all there!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie, it was Maggie.
No we shan't. Yoink!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie, this is so sweet. But I can't possibly go now... the sink is full of dirty dishes, the trash needs to be taken out, the living room is a mess...
Marge, I can see you withholding sex or withholding cake. But withholding sexy cake? I know we have to move past this, but I don't see how.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie, what do you say we go to bed? You, me and the cake?
Do you like guys who are... attractive?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie, you look good!
Oh, you're right.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Homie... Put down your magazine for a minute...
Go to hell.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: How was your day at work, dear?
Guess I forgot to put the fog lights in...

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I better pull over and play it safe.
Marge, you're missing the point. The individual doesn't matter. It was a team effort and I was the one who came up with the whole team idea. Me.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I can't believe Otto picked up a 7-10 split. He's phenomenal!
Actually, those were Carl's shirts.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I can't believe you're gonna spend another weekend with him.
Pretty good. Thanks for asking.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I don't know what happened. I saw you and I went for the brake but I hit the accelerator!
But you do believe it, right?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I don't know what to believe anymore.
Well, uh... The one place the cameras can't see is right here in our backyard so I'm charging people to do whatever they want -- isn't that wonderful?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I don't see what's so wonderful.
Well, something did.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I don't want you stalking anyone tonight.
Marge, I realized something when I was trapped under all that rubble: marriage is the real roller coaster. I'm just glad I have you as my safety bar.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I forgive you my darling. Get well.
Probably misses his old glasses.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I guess we could get more involved in Bart's activities. But then I'd be afraid of smothering him.
Way ahead of you, Marge -- I just ordered a series of tapes on saving money. They should get here soon. I paid a bundle for over-night delivery.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I have a book from the library with the same information!
I'll never eat turkey again. Marge, we got any ham?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I hereby declare Thanksgiving dinner officially over!
Okay, we're watching.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I hope we're not spoiling them.
You know, we could get out of these stupid things if you'd just tell the judge you're a bad mother. And you don't even have to say "bad." It could be "negligent" or "unfit" or "drugged-up.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I just can't do that, Homer. It's a matter of principle. And I need you to support me in this.
Look, Marge, I know I was supposed to yell at that Priest, but he's so cool. He plays drums in a band with a bunch of other priests!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I knew they'd try to convert you! That's what they do! Well I'm not having another twelve kids.
Do you know what I just learned? My job is the reason I get those checks every week! And now that I'm demoted, the checks have gotten smaller! Not in physical size, but--

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I know! I know!
Do I ever! It's five years later and I still think I'm a chicken. I'm a chicken, Marge.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I know, I know.
I love that dog.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I love him, too. G'night.
I love you, Marge.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I love you too, Homie.
Marge, there's just too much pressure... what with my job, the kids, traffic snarls, political strife at home and abroad... but I promise you, the second all those things go away, we'll have sex.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I simply can't wait that long. Maybe we should get some help... How 'bout a book?
Huh? Well... it's all ours!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I still can't believe how inexpensive it was.
Marge, dogs love the outdoors.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I think he needs a dog house.
That's the plan.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I think it's nice we're doing something Maggie will enjoy for once. Besides, I'm sure Storytown Village is also fun for everyone... from 8, to... God only knows.
Okay, but just for a minute. We want to hit the candle store, Fudgerama, the Zipper Hall of Fame, Snow Globe World, and The Taj Meatball.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I think that Shiva used to be Paul Bunyan.
It's go time.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I was just making Christmas cookies. But since you don't believe in Christmas anymore, I guess you don't want any.
Oh. Oh. Oh. Oh! Great! Listen, I know it looks bad. But all I can tell you is I destroyed that car for all the right reasons.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I'd like to believe you...

Marge, I'm gonna miss you so much. And it's not just the sex... it's also the food preparation... your skill with stains of all kinds. But mostly, I'll miss how lucky you make me feel each and every morning.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I'll miss you too Homie.
Oh, Marge. What a pleasant surprise.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I'm at a rest stop south of Springfield. I know, you're sorry now. Then you'll buy me some Kwik-E-Mart flowers, maybe a box of candy where half the pieces mysteriously have "testing bites," and a week later you'll be back to your old thoughtless self.

I'm not sure what happened. I was kidnapped, then tortured, then I fell into a surprisingly sound sleep. When I awoke, I felt refreshed. Then I was blindfolded, and two sobbing trolls threw me out of a van onto our lawn.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I'm just happy you're back. Now let's get that chain off you.
You know Marge, joining the reserves was the best thing I ever did. I feel good about myself, I'm helping my country, and later, I'm gonna get Gilligan's autograph.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I'm so proud of you, Homie.
Yes. We'll send the eye.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I'm sure he'll offer us a fair reward. And then we'll make him double it.
What up, Marge?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: I'm watching a videotape that could change our lives.

Now, Marge, you can't blame all of Bart's problems on your one little speech. If anything turned him bad, it's that time you let him wear a bathing suit instead of underwear. And let's not forget your little speech...

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Isn't there anything we can do?
No one steals my kids... except me... from that theme park jail... that I never told you about... except I guess I just did... we're all caught up now... let's go!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: It all makes sense now.
Wait till Flanders gets a load of this.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: It all seems so expensive...
No, a guy at work seems not to like me. I guess it's not much when you look at real problems in the world like major league umpires not using instant replay.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: It's big to you. Would you like a "get well" pork chop?
I just have one question, my darling: what did you do with all the ice cream that was on all those sticks?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: It's in that dumpster.
I'm confused! Which is it?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: It's no! His old bike is fine!
I don't need to know, Marge. You deserve to have your secrets.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: It's not a secret. It's a funny story.

Oh, what's the big deal? Bart didn't like his presents. So what? It's not like he gives us such great gifts. Remember that maple leaf ironed between the sheets of wax paper? What was that? That was crap.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: It's not just the presents -- the kids don't appreciate me anymore. They'd rather hang out with their friends than with their mom.
Oh man, this is great. The most evil man in town is in our power. He will do my bidding... at that fantasy football auction. And anything else my limited imagination can come up with.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Just because Mr. Burns was mean to you, that doesn't give you the right to abuse him when he's helpless.
Wow, eye of the tiger, mouth of a teamster. To think of all the time I wasted on you... uh, well, not wasted... I love you.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Lemme give my special little winner a big, big hug.
You mean --?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Let's do it, Homer!
Look, Lisa. It glows. Oooo.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Let's forget about the band contest and just have fun at the State Fair.
I'll bet somewhere there's a horse drinking coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Live from New York it's Saturday Night!
You know what's great about you, Marge? After all these years you can still shinny up the donut, and then pull me up after you.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Look! A shooting star!
Not with that attitude.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Look, maybe this whole thing will blow over.
I turned it off.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Looks like the red light's on.
Woo hoo! Off the hook!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Looks like this is all me.
Oh, no?! Well, if Homer Simpson wants his ten-year-old son working in a burlesque house, then Homer Simpson's ten-year-old son is going to work in a burlesque house! That's...

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Maison Derriere"?! I can't believe there's a place like that in our wholesome little town. Homer, did you know it was a burlesque house when you sent Bart to work there?
Three fifteen p.m., May 18th! That's when the Rapture will be!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: May eighteenth? That's one week from today!
I am so stoked about Lenny's party. He said he's gonna make a surprise announcement!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Maybe he's getting married!
Yeah, what do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: My husband by my side.
Oh, I can't believe those goons muscled me out of my grease business. I've been muscled out of everything I've ever done, including my muscle-for-hire business.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: My poor Homie. Couldn't you try some other far-out money-making scheme?
Hi, this is Jerry Maguire. Show me the message. Show me the message.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: Nnno, that stinks. Let me try one.
Push her down, son.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: No one's going anywhere. We're going to clean the whole house from top to bottom.
What about partays?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: No partays, no shindigs, no keggers, no hootenannies, no mixers, no raves, no box socials...
Of course I know!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: No peeking. I'm wai-ting.
What? They had a picnic last week.

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: No they didn't. You just brought a bucket of chicken to church.
But you learned! You grew!

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: No! You should never raise your hand to a child. Just leave the crust on their sandwiches. They'll get the message.
Because I knocked you up?

dialogue.speaker: Marge Simpson
dialogue.text: No, because I love you.
Was it the kiss?
